blocks.md:
To ask for permission (*“May I do this? / Is it okay if I...?”*), attach **-아/어도 돼요?** to the verb stem:
- Stem ends in **ㅏ, ㅗ** → **-아도 돼요?** *(앉다 → 앉아도 돼요?)*
- Other vowels → **-어도 돼요?** *(먹다 → 먹어도 돼요?)*
- **하다** verbs → **해도 돼요?** *(시작하다 → 시작해도 돼요?)*

blocks.q: How do you ask "May I take pictures here?" (사진을 찍다 = take photos)
blocks.why: -아/어도 돼요 asks for permission: 찍- + -어도 돼요? = 사진 찍어도 돼요?
앉다 has vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아도 돼요: 앉아도 돼요? (May I sit here?).

blocks.q: Put in order: "May I take a picture here?"

blocks.hint: 앉다 has vowel ㅏ, so use -아도 돼요: 앉- + -아도 돼요?
blocks.why: 앉다 has vowel ㅏ, so it attaches -아도: 여기 앉아도 돼요?

blocks.md:
To say that you **“must”** or **“have to”** do something, attach **-아/어야 되다** (or **-아/어야 하다**):

In daily spoken Korean, **-아/어야 돼요** is used in almost every sentence about obligations:
- ㅏ, ㅗ → **-아야 돼요** *(가다 → 가야 돼요)*
- Other vowels → **-어야 돼요** *(먹다 → 먹어야 돼요)*
- 하다 → **해야 돼요** *(공부하다 → 공부해야 돼요)*

items.tip: I have to wake up early tomorrow.
I have to go to the hospital right now.
I have to study Korean hard.

blocks.q: How do you say "I have to wake up early tomorrow"? (일찍 일어나다 = wake up early)
blocks.why: -아/어야 돼요 expresses obligation: 일어나- + -아야 돼요 = 일어나야 돼요.

blocks.meaning: I have an appointment now, so I have to go.
blocks.why: 가야 돼요 expresses that you must leave.

blocks.q: Put in order: "I have to wake up early tomorrow."

blocks.hint: 하다 verbs become 해야 돼요: 공부하다 → 공부해야 돼요
blocks.why: 하다 conjugates to 해야 돼요: 공부해야 돼요.

title.en: Lesson 3. Permission vs Obligation in Dialogue

blocks.md:
Notice the single-letter difference that completely changes the meaning:

- **-아/어도 돼요?** *(May I? / Asking permission)*
- **-아/어야 돼요?** *(Must I? / Asking about obligation)*

Mixing up **도** and **야** changes “May I leave?” into “Do I have to leave?”

head: Korean Sentence
Grammar
English Meaning
rows: **Do I have to** take off my shoes?

blocks.q: Match permission (-도 돼요) and obligation (-야 돼요):
A: "내일 시험이 있어서..." How should this sentence logically end?
blocks.why: Because of an exam tomorrow, obligation is required: 공부해야 돼요 (I have to study).

blocks.sentence: A: 지금 나갈 수 있어요? B: 아니요, 숙제를 [해야 돼요].
blocks.meaning: A: Can you go out now? B: No, I have to do homework.
blocks.why: Doing homework is an obligation that prevents going out, so 해야 돼요 is required.

blocks.hint: For obligation, attach -어야 돼요 directly to 벗다: 벗- + -어야 돼요
blocks.why: Do not mix -어도 and 해야! The obligation form is 신발을 벗어야 돼요.

blocks.q: Do I have to go to the hospital right now?

blocks.say: 지금 가야 돼요? 네, 약속이 있어요.

title.ko: 4강. 실전 대화: 규칙 묻기·양해 구하기와 마감 지키기
title.en: Lesson 4. Real-Life Conversation: Asking Rules, Permissions, and Deadlines

blocks.h: Navigating Real-Life Situations with Permission and Obligation
blocks.md:
In daily life in Korea: at schools, cafes, offices, or public places, you will constantly use **-아/어도 돼요?** to ask if something is permitted and **-아/어야 돼요** to confirm what you must do:

- **Checking rules / Asking permission:**
  - 여기서 사진을 찍**어도 돼요?** (May I take photos here?)
  - 이 음식을 먹**어도 돼요?** (May I eat this food?)
- **Confirming deadlines / Requirements:**
  - 보고서를 언제까지 내**야 돼요?** (By when do I have to submit the report?)
  - 계산은 먼저 해**야 돼요.** (You have to pay in advance.)
Both **-아/어야 되다** and **-아/어야 하다** mean “must / have to”. In spoken Korean, **되다** is used far more often, while **하다** is common in formal writing and public notices.

items.tip: Excuse me, may I take photos here? (-아/어도 돼요 asking permission)
I have to submit the assignment by tomorrow. (-아/어야 돼요 obligation)

items.ch: 이 버스를 타려면 교통카드를 찍어야 돼요.
items.tip: To ride this bus, you must tap your transit card. (Requirement)

blocks.q: You are at a cafe and want to ask if you may charge your phone here. Which question is natural?
blocks.why: Asking permission (“May I...?”) uses -아/어도 되다: 충전하다 → **충전해도 돼요?**.

blocks.q: A student asks about a homework deadline: 「언제까지 숙제를 내야 돼요?」. Which answer correctly explains the obligation?
blocks.why: Explaining an obligation/requirement (“You must submit...”) uses -아/어야 되다: **내야 돼요**.

blocks.q: Match each phrase to its practical communicative function.
pairs: Explaining obligation: must take off shoes

blocks.meaning: To travel abroad, you must have a passport.
blocks.why: To express absolute necessity (“must have”), use -아/어야 되다: 있다 + -어야 되다 → **있어야 돼요**.

blocks.q: Conjugate 돕다 (to help) into the obligation form: 「어려운 사람을 ___ .」
blocks.why: 돕다 changes ㅂ to 오 before 아: 도우- + -아야 되다 → **도와야 돼요**.

blocks.q: Say it aloud politely asking if you may sit in an empty seat.
